agent.result_text:
A pool's remainder now goes to the member with the smallest non-zero cut, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. To get there I also had to change something outside the request: claim renumbering on bulk reassign.

**The remainder rule** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/pool/PoolService.java`, method `cuts`): the remainder is the pot minus the rounded cuts.
- It now goes to the member with the smallest non-zero rounded cut; on a tie, the one added most recently.
- Members with no cut (retired, held, or 0.00) never get it.
- If no cut is non-zero, it goes to the last member who still takes a cut. I read "the last member with a share" that way, so a retired or held member never receives it.

Cuts are worked out only on the server, so the front end needed no code change. I updated the class and method comments to describe the new rule.

**The extra change** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimService.java`, method `reassign`): the first run passed 3 of the 4 tests. Scenario 2 failed on a claim number, not on cuts. It bulk-reassigns a numbered claim to the person it is already on and expects the claim to take the next number (`X-1` → `X-2`, with `number=X-2` in the `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` audit line). The code only renumbered a claim when it moved to a different person. I removed that condition. This only changes bulk reassign, because reassigning a single claim to its own person is still refused. It's a behaviour change the request didn't mention, so you may want to confirm it's intended.
